title.ja: Firecracker: Lambda と Fargate の下で動く microVM
title.en: Firecracker: The MicroVM under Lambda and Fargate

sources.title: Firecracker README (v1.17.0)
supports: Firecracker is a virtual machine monitor that uses KVM to create and run microVMs, and excludes unnecessary devices and guest-facing functionality
It was developed at Amazon Web Services to accelerate the speed and efficiency of services like AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate, and is open source under Apache 2.0
One Firecracker process exposes an API endpoint; the defaults are 1 vCPU and 128 MiB
What the API can configure, including rate limiters for virtio devices, a vsock, an entropy device, pmem, memory hotplug
The jailer applies a cgroup and namespace barrier and drops privileges
Tested platforms are EC2 .metal instances of Intel, AMD and Graviton generations with host kernels 5.10, 6.1 and 6.18; 8th generation Intel only with 6.1 or 6.18
The security of microVMs depends on a well configured Linux host

sources.title: Firecracker Specification (v1.17.0)
supports: On M5D.metal and M6G.metal: the VMM starts within 8 CPU ms, with wall-clock from 6 ms to 60 ms
For 1 vCPU and 128 MiB with the Firecracker-tuned kernel: VMM memory overhead <= 5 MiB, depending on workload and configuration
<= 125 ms from the InstanceStart call to the start of /sbin/init, measured with the serial console disabled and a minimal kernel and root file system
Guest CPU performance > 95% of bare metal, marked integration test pending
The API conforms to the in-tree OpenAPI specification

sources.title: Firecracker Design (v1.17.0)
supports: Each Firecracker process encapsulates one and only one microVM; threads are API, VMM and one per vCPU
Up to 32 vCPUs; 5 microVMs per host core per second with a minimal kernel, one vCPU and 128 MiB
Network devices are backed by TAP devices and block devices by files on the host
All vCPU threads are considered to run malicious code once started; Firecracker does not filter network traffic
Rate limiters are two token buckets, operations per second and bandwidth
Seccomp filters are installed by Firecracker; the jailer sets up cgroups and chroot, drops privileges, and execs Firecracker
In production builds the serial console is not exposed

sources.title: Firecracker FAQ (v1.17.0)
supports: Lambda launched in November 2014 with per-customer EC2 instances for isolation
Firecracker started from crosvm and is written in Rust
Only 6 emulated devices are named: virtio-net, virtio-balloon, virtio-block, virtio-vsock, serial console, and a minimal keyboard controller
Guest and host must have the same CPU architecture
Firecracker does not support guest reboot; on x86 `reboot` with reboot=k ends the process
The serial console is disabled by default for boot time
sources.note: The FAQ's list of six devices is shorter than the README's feature list of the same tag, which also names an entropy device and pmem.

sources.title: Firecracker Charter (v1.17.0)
supports: Mission: secure, multi-tenant, minimal-overhead execution of container and function workloads
Tenets: built-in security, light-weight virtualization, minimalist in features, compute oversubscription

sources.title: Firecracker LICENSE and NOTICE (v1.17.0)
supports: Apache License 2.0; portions from Chromium OS under a BSD-style license; the release bundle includes libseccomp under LGPLv2.1

sources.title: Getting Started with Firecracker (v1.17.0)
supports: Firecracker requires read/write access to /dev/kvm and supports x86_64 and aarch64 Linux
The guide suggests an EC2 c5.metal instance and says EC2 only supports KVM on .metal instance types
The commands that fetch a kernel and an Ubuntu rootfs from the project's CI bucket, add an SSH key, and build an ext4 image
The TAP device, 172.16.0.1/30, NAT, the guest MAC 06:00:AC:10:00:02 and the guest address 172.16.0.2
The API calls of a boot: logger, boot-source, drives, network-interfaces, actions InstanceStart; requests are handled asynchronously
--config-file configures and starts a microVM without API requests
The integration tests enforce the specification as measured on EC2 .metal instances
sources.note: The statement about .metal conflicts with the EC2 user guide's nested virtualization page read the same day.

sources.title: Firecracker development machine setup (v1.17.0)
supports: Development needs a bare-metal machine or a virtual machine with nested virtualization; the AWS section uses bare metal instances

sources.title: The Firecracker Jailer (v1.17.0)
supports: The jailer's arguments and its steps: close file descriptors, clean the environment, copy the binary into a chroot, set resource limits, create cgroups, pivot_root, mknod /dev/net/tun and /dev/kvm, join a network namespace, drop privileges, exec
Copying the binary ensures the process shares no memory with another Firecracker process

sources.title: Production Host Setup Recommendations (v1.17.0)
supports: Firecracker should be started with the jailer in production, or under constraints at least as restrictive
Each Firecracker process should correspond to a workload of a single tenant
Firecracker cannot mitigate the host's hardware vulnerabilities; SMT and kernel samepage merging should be disabled for tenant separation
Firecracker does not filter guest traffic; a rule dropping packets from TAP devices to 169.254.169.254 is given
The serial device should not be enabled in production

sources.title: Firecracker Snapshotting (v1.17.0)
supports: A snapshot is a guest memory file and a microVM state file; disk files are managed by the user
Loading maps the memory file MAP_PRIVATE, so pages load on demand and writes go to anonymous memory
Pause, Resume and CreateSnapshot only after boot; LoadSnapshot only before configuration
Diff snapshots are in developer preview
Resuming the same snapshot more than once is considered insecure without a mechanism for uniqueness; VMGenID reseeds the guest kernel's PRNG on Linux 5.18 and later
Network connectivity is not guaranteed after resume

sources.title: Firecracker kernel support policy (v1.17.0)
supports: Supported host kernels 5.10, 6.1, 6.18 and guest kernels 5.10, 6.1, 6.18, with minimum end of support dates

sources.title: Firecracker API request documents: actions, patch-network-interface (v1.17.0)
supports: InstanceStart can only be successfully called once
SendCtrlAltDel is Intel and AMD only
Rate limiters of a network interface can be updated after boot with PATCH; a zero-sized bucket disables a limit

sources.title: Firecracker API specification, Swagger 2.0 (v1.17.0)
supports: The paths, operationIds, success statuses and definitions that spec/firecracker-v1.17.0.subset.json is cut from; sha256 473a0a392927b407834b341bf5fbc7925524fedaf9d925e1bbbafb6a1f48c671
machine-config, boot-source, drives and network-interfaces are pre-boot only; vcpu_count is 1 to 32; a snapshot needs the Paused state
The transport is a Unix domain socket

sources.title: Firecracker: Lightweight Virtualization for Serverless Applications (NSDI '20)
supports: Lambda first isolated functions with Linux containers and customers with virtual machines
Containers trade security against compatibility through the syscalls they allow; language VM isolation was unsuitable because Lambda and Fargate run arbitrary binaries
Firecracker has no BIOS, cannot boot arbitrary kernels, emulates no legacy devices nor PCI, and supports no VM migration (as of the paper)
Each Lambda worker runs hundreds or thousands of microVMs, each a slot for one function and one concurrent invocation, reused for serial invocations
A pool of pre-booted microVMs hides boot latency; slots lived at most 12 hours
Measured with Firecracker v0.20.0 on m5d.metal: memory overhead around 3 MB; boot figures; block and network throughput
The seccomp profile then allowed 24 syscalls and 30 ioctls
Lambda migrated to Firecracker on EC2 bare metal instances starting in 2018
sources.note: Published February 2020 about Firecracker v0.20.0 and the Lambda of that time.

sources.title: Firecracker - Lightweight Virtualization for Serverless Computing (AWS News Blog)
supports: AWS's 2018 statement that Firecracker powers Lambda and Fargate, launches a microVM in as little as 125 ms and uses about 5 MiB per microVM

sources.title: Announcing the Firecracker Open Source Technology (AWS Open Source Blog, 27 Nov 2018)
supports: Fargate tasks previously ran in a dedicated EC2 VM each and, as of the post, execute on Firecracker microVMs on EC2 bare metal instances

sources.title: Security Overview of AWS Lambda (AWS Whitepaper)
supports: Lambda Workers are bare metal EC2 Nitro instances in a separate account, with one or more microVMs created by Firecracker; a Worker's lease is at most 14 hours
Execution environments are never reused across function versions or customers; one environment is reused between invocations of the same version
The isolation technologies listed: cgroups, namespaces, seccomp-bpf, iptables, chroot, Firecracker rate limiting
sources.note: Last revision listed in the document: December 27, 2022. Its SnapStart paragraph is older than the developer guide. The HTML pages of the whitepaper redirected to the Lambda developer guide; the PDF was read.

sources.title: Serverless and Containers - Logical Separation on AWS
supports: AWS describes the isolation of Lambda and Fargate as layers: bare metal instances on Nitro, then Firecracker

sources.title: Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle
supports: Lambda invokes a function in an execution environment, a secure and isolated runtime environment

sources.title: Improving startup performance with Lambda SnapStart
supports: Lambda takes a Firecracker microVM snapshot of the memory and disk state of the initialized execution environment when a version is published, and resumes new environments from it
Supported runtimes: Java 11 and later, Python 3.12 and later, .NET 8 and later; other managed runtimes such as nodejs24.x are not supported
One snapshot is the initial state of many environments, so unique content must be generated after initialization; network connections are not guaranteed

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Lambda (default) uses Firecracker MicroVM technology to isolate execution environments on shared fleets; Managed Instances use containers on EC2 Nitro instances rather than Firecracker

sources.title: Security for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Containers are not a security boundary; the capacity provider is

sources.title: Amazon ECS security considerations for when to use Fargate
supports: Fargate runs each task in a hardware virtualization environment

sources.title: Amazon ECS task IAM role
supports: Each task on Fargate has its own isolation boundary and does not share the underlying kernel, CPU, memory or elastic network interface with another task

sources.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs
supports: Lambda MicroVMs are serverless environments with VM-level isolation, started from snapshots, suspended and resumed, delivered through Firecracker virtualization
They are meant for running user or AI-generated code: interactive environments, sandboxes, multi-tenant CI

sources.title: AWS introduces Lambda MicroVMs (What's New, 22 Jun 2026)
supports: Posted June 22, 2026; available in Regions including Asia Pacific (Tokyo)

sources.title: Use nested virtualization to run hypervisors in Amazon EC2 instances
supports: Nested virtualization runs KVM and Hyper-V inside virtual (non-bare-metal) EC2 instances at no additional cost
Supported types: M7i, M7i-flex, M8i, M8id, M8i-flex, C7i, C7i-flex, C8i, C8id, C8i-flex, R7i, R7iz, R8i, R8id, R8i-flex, X8i, I7i, I7ie
It is enabled with the NestedVirtualization CPU option at launch or on a stopped instance; describe-instance-types lists the types
AWS recommends evaluating bare metal for performance-sensitive workloads; the customer secures the hypervisor and nested virtual machines

sources.title: How Workers works - Cloudflare Workers docs
supports: One runtime instance runs hundreds or thousands of isolates; an isolate starts around a hundred times faster than a Node process on a container or virtual machine and uses an order of magnitude less memory at startup

sources.title: Security model - Cloudflare Workers docs
supports: Tenants are isolated with V8 isolates, not processes nor VMs; the process around them is sandboxed with namespaces and seccomp with no file system or network access
V8 has a wider attack surface than virtual machines, in Cloudflare's own words, and Workers has its own Spectre strategy

sources.title: Vercel Sandbox
supports: Each sandbox runs in a Firecracker microVM with its own file system and network

definition.ja: KVM の上で microVM を動かす、オープンソースの仮想マシンモニター。AWS が Lambda と Fargate のために作り、Apache 2.0 で公開している。プロセス 1 つが microVM 1 つを受け持つ。
definition.en: An open-source virtual machine monitor that runs microVMs on KVM. AWS built it for Lambda and Fargate and publishes it under Apache 2.0. One process is one microVM.

definition.ja: デバイスを最小限に絞った小さな仮想マシン。自分のカーネルを持つので、分離の境界はハードウェア仮想化になる。
definition.en: A small virtual machine with a minimal set of devices. It has its own kernel, so its isolation boundary is hardware virtualization.

definition.ja: 仮想マシンにデバイスを見せ、ゲストが外に出ようとする操作を処理するプログラム。Firecracker や QEMU がこれにあたる。
definition.en: The program that presents devices to a virtual machine and handles what the guest does when it leaves guest mode. Firecracker and QEMU are VMMs.

definition.ja: Linux カーネルの仮想化機能。CPU の仮想化支援機能を使い、/dev/kvm を通じて VMM に仮想マシンを作らせる。
definition.en: The virtualization feature of the Linux kernel. It uses the CPU's virtualization extensions and lets a VMM create virtual machines through /dev/kvm.

definition.ja: Firecracker に付属するプログラム。chroot、cgroup、名前空間を用意し、権限を落としてから Firecracker を起動する。
definition.en: A program shipped with Firecracker. It sets up a chroot, cgroups and namespaces, drops privileges, and then execs Firecracker.

definition.ja: 仮想マシンの中でさらに仮想マシンを動かすこと。EC2 では一部の Intel のインスタンスタイプで、CPU オプションとして有効にできる。
definition.en: Running a virtual machine inside a virtual machine. On EC2 it is a CPU option of some Intel instance types.

summary.ja: Firecracker を 1 度も起動していない。クライアントが本物の v1.17.0 と話せること、自作のサーバーの断り方が本物と一致すること、deploy/ のスクリプト、ゲストの中の Node.js とサーバー、起動時間、スナップショットは未確認。
summary.en: Firecracker was never started. That the client talks to the real v1.17.0, that this book's fake server refuses what the real one refuses, the scripts in deploy/, Node.js and the server inside the guest, boot times and snapshots are unconfirmed.

resume.ja: Linux と KVM のあるマシンで vp run firecracker:kit:build の dist/kit を置き、bash deploy/prepare.sh、sudo bash deploy/tap.sh up、sudo work/firecracker --api-sock /tmp/firecracker.socket、別の端末で sudo work/node/bin/node boot.mjs を順に実行する。断られたリクエストのステータスと fault_message を test/support/fake-firecracker.ts の規則と比べて直し、表示された 3 つの時間を記録する。続けて --snapshot を試す。
resume.en: On a machine with Linux and KVM, place dist/kit from vp run firecracker:kit:build and run in order: bash deploy/prepare.sh, sudo bash deploy/tap.sh up, sudo work/firecracker --api-sock /tmp/firecracker.socket, and in another terminal sudo work/node/bin/node boot.mjs. Compare the status and fault_message of any refused request with the rules in test/support/fake-firecracker.ts and correct them, and record the three durations printed. Then try --snapshot.

summary.ja: nested virtualization を有効にした c7i.large で /dev/kvm が現れ、Firecracker が動くことは未確認。Firecracker のプロジェクトがテストしているのは .metal だけで、手引きは EC2 では .metal でしか KVM を使えないと書いている（EC2 のガイドと食い違う）。
summary.en: That /dev/kvm appears on a c7i.large with nested virtualization enabled, and that Firecracker runs there, is unconfirmed. The Firecracker project tests only .metal, and its quickstart says EC2 supports KVM only on .metal (which disagrees with the EC2 guide).

resume.ja: vp run net:infra:deploy、vp run firecracker:infra:deploy -c run=true、vp run firecracker:kit:publish のあと Session Manager で入り、ls -l /dev/kvm の結果から記録する。動かなければ instanceType を変えるか、.metal で試した結果と並べる。終わったら firecracker:kit:empty と firecracker:infra:destroy。
resume.en: After vp run net:infra:deploy, vp run firecracker:infra:deploy -c run=true and vp run firecracker:kit:publish, enter through Session Manager and record from the output of ls -l /dev/kvm onward. If it does not work, change instanceType or compare with a .metal instance. Finish with firecracker:kit:empty and firecracker:infra:destroy.
